subs.name: 过氧化氢（双氧水）
subs.note: 无色液体，遇催化剂迅速分解放出氧。
subs.noteEn: Colourless liquid; rapidly decomposes to release O₂ over a catalyst.

subs.name: 二氧化锰（黑色粉末）
subs.note: 作催化剂，加快分解而自身不消耗。
subs.noteEn: Catalyst; speeds decomposition without being consumed.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 能使带火星木条复燃，是收集目标。
subs.noteEn: Relights a glowing splint; the gas being collected.

oneLiner: 双氧水加二氧化锰催化，常温分解放出氧气。
oneLinerEn: Hydrogen peroxide decomposes at room temperature over MnO₂ catalyst.
detail: 这是初中三种实验室制氧路线里唯一不需要加热的一条，所以发生装置走“固液不加热”那一类（与制 CO₂、制 H₂ 同一套，见「常见气体的实验室制取」）：锥形瓶里放二氧化锰，从分液漏斗滴加过氧化氢，拧着活塞控制滴速就能得到平稳气流，比一次性倒进去要好控制得多。为什么二氧化锰写在箭头上方而不是写进反应物？因为它是催化剂，反应前后质量和化学性质都不变，不参与配平；实验结束后往残留物里加足水溶解、过滤、洗涤、干燥，回收到的二氧化锰质量与加入时相同（氯化钾溶于水而二氧化锰不溶，这一步同时是“催化剂质量不变”最直接的验证）。从化合价看它是一类很有意思的反应：过氧化氢中氧是 −1 价，分解后一部分降到 −2（进入 H₂O）、一部分升到 0（变成 O₂），同一元素自己既升高又降低，这叫歧化；所以 2 分子过氧化氢只给 1 分子氧气，68 g 纯过氧化氢对应 32 g 氧气，别按“一个分子出一个氧”去算。三个易错处：一是把催化剂当生成物写到等号右边；二是以为只有二氧化锰能催化——氯化铁溶液、土豆和肝脏里的过氧化氢酶同样能催化，说明催化剂不唯一，而酶只在体温附近高效、高温会变性；三是浓度，医用双氧水约 3%，靠同样分解放出的新生态氧杀灭厌氧菌，浓度过高反而灼伤皮肤，做实验也不要擅自换成高浓度。最后记住检验方法：导管口气体能使带火星的木条复燃才是氧气，验满要把带火星木条放在集气瓶口。
detailEn: This is the only one of the three lab routes to oxygen that needs no heating, so the generator belongs to the solid-plus-liquid, no-heat family shared with CO2 and H2 (see Preparing Gases in the Lab): MnO2 sits in the flask and H2O2 is added from a dropping funnel, where turning the stopcock sets a steady stream instead of one violent burst. MnO2 is written above the arrow, not among the reactants, because a catalyst is unchanged in mass and chemical properties and takes no part in balancing; dissolving the residue in water, filtering, washing and drying recovers the same mass of MnO2 (KCl dissolves, MnO2 does not), which is the cleanest hands-on proof that a catalyst is not consumed. In oxidation-state terms this is a disproportionation: oxygen in H2O2 is -1, and after decomposition part of it drops to -2 in water while part rises to 0 in O2, so two formula units give only one oxygen molecule - 68 g of pure H2O2 yields 32 g of O2, not the one-to-one a careless reading suggests. Three common mistakes: putting the catalyst on the product side; assuming only MnO2 works, when FeCl3 solution and the catalase in potato or liver are just as effective, which shows catalysts are not unique and that enzymes only work near body temperature and are destroyed by heat; and ignoring concentration - medical hydrogen peroxide is about 3 percent, disinfecting anaerobes through the same freshly released oxygen, while stronger solutions burn skin. For testing, a glowing splint relighting at the delivery tube proves oxygen; for a full check hold the glowing splint at the mouth of the jar.

subs.name: 高锰酸钾（紫黑色固体）
subs.note: 加热即分解，实验室制氧原料。
subs.noteEn: Decomposes on heating; a lab source of O₂.

subs.name: 氧气
subs.note: 供收集，使带火星木条复燃。

oneLiner: 高锰酸钾加热分解，放出氧气。
oneLinerEn: Potassium permanganate decomposes on heating, releasing O₂.
detail: 高锰酸钾法是三种制氧路线中的“固体加热”类，与氯酸钾法同一套装置：试管口要略向下倾斜，防止冷凝水倒流使灼热的管底炸裂；试管口要塞一小团棉花，作用是挡住随氧气流冲出紫黑色粉末——粉末进导管会堵塞、进水槽会把水染成紫红。操作上先左右移动试管均匀预热，再固定药品部位强热；用排水法收集时要等气泡连续均匀冒出才收集，因为一开始排出的是试管里的空气；实验结束的顺序必须记牢：先把导管移出水面，再熄灭酒精灯，反了就会因管内的气压降低把水槽里的冷水倒吸进灼热试管。这条反应的化合价并不安分：锰从 +7 一分降到 +6（K₂MnO₄，锰酸钾）一分降到 +4（MnO₂），氧则从 −2 升到 0，所以 2 mol 高锰酸钾（约 316 g）只得 1 mol 氧气（32 g），产氧效率明显低于氯酸钾（每 122.5 g 就给 24 g 氧）。看颜色就能判断反应进度：紫黑色晶体逐渐变成墨绿与黑色混杂的残留。顺便分清两件事：本反应生成的二氧化锰是产物，而「氯酸钾受热分解」里二氧化锰是催化剂，高锰酸钾自己绝不能充当氯酸钾的催化剂（因为它一受热就分解，产物里多出的锰酸钾与二氧化锰才是真正起催化作用的东西）。稀的高锰酸钾溶液紫红色、氧化性很强，在分析中作氧化剂滴定时它自己就能当指示剂——终点是被还原到几乎无色或出现淡粉色，不需要另加指示剂；生活中它也被用作消毒与水果保鲜剂，但浓度必须很稀。
detailEn: The permanganate route is the heat-a-solid member of the three lab preparations of oxygen, so it shares the apparatus with potassium chlorate: tilt the tube mouth slightly downward so condensed water cannot run back onto the hot bottom and crack it, and plug the mouth with a loose wad of cotton to stop the dark violet powder from riding the oxygen stream into the delivery tube, where it would clog it or dye the water trough purple. Warm the tube evenly by sliding it over the flame before heating the charge directly, and with drainage collection wait until bubbles come over steadily and continuously, because the first bubbles are just the air that was in the tube. Remember the shutdown order: draw the delivery tube out of the water before killing the lamp, otherwise the cooling tube sucks cold water back onto hot glass. The oxidation states here are restless: manganese at +7 splits, part dropping to +6 in potassium manganate and part to +4 in MnO2, while oxygen climbs from -2 to 0, so 2 mol of KMnO4 (about 316 g) give only 1 mol of O2 (32 g) - a clearly poorer yield than KClO3, which delivers 24 g of oxygen per 122.5 g. Colour tells you how far the reaction has gone: the violet-black crystals turn into a greenish-black mixture. Keep two things apart: the MnO2 formed here is a product, whereas in Potassium Chlorate Decomposition MnO2 is the catalyst, and KMnO4 can never serve as that catalyst since it decomposes itself first. Dilute permanganate solution is strongly oxidising and useful as its own indicator in redox titrations - the end point shows as loss of the violet or a faint pink - and at very low concentration it is also used as a disinfectant and fruit preservative.

subs.name: 二氧化锰
subs.note: 催化剂，降低反应温度、加快速率。
subs.noteEn: Catalyst; lowers temperature and speeds the reaction.

oneLiner: 氯酸钾在二氧化锰催化并加热下分解放氧。
oneLinerEn: Potassium chlorate decomposes with MnO₂ and heat to give O₂.
detail: 这是初中实验室制氧气的第三种药品路线，也是「催化剂」概念最标准的载体。操作上与高锰酸钾法几乎一样：试管口略向下倾斜防冷凝水倒流，导管刚伸入试管内一点即可，用排水法收集。差别在药品本身：氯酸钾单独加热到约 356 ℃ 熔化之后才缓慢放氧，混入二氧化锰并磨匀后在两三百度就明显反应，所以二氧化锰写在箭头上方作条件，不进方程式的配平。它在这里确确实实是催化剂：反应前后质量和化学性质都不变，结束后加足水溶解、过滤、洗涤、干燥就能把它回收（氯化钾溶于水而二氧化锰不溶），这是“催化剂质量不变”最直接的验证。三个高频易错处：一、不能拿高锰酸钾代替二氧化锰——高锰酸钾自己分解也会放氧，但它的产物里多出锰酸钾与二氧化锰，真正起催化作用的是后生成的二氧化锰；二、氯酸钾是强氧化剂，混入炭粉、硫或纸屑后研磨、受热都可能猛燃甚至爆炸，只能与二氧化锰配伍；三、常见错写是把方程式不配平就交，或者把催化剂当生成物写到右边。工业上氯酸钾用于火柴头与烟火，学生实验只用极少量，多余的药品不得倒回原瓶（见「药品的存放与容器选择」）。
detailEn: This is the third of the school oxygen preparations and the standard carrier of the catalyst idea. The handling is the permanganate recipe unchanged: mouth tilted slightly down so condensate cannot run back, delivery tube barely inside the tube, collection over water. The difference is in the drug. Potassium chlorate melts near 356 °C and only then gives oxygen slowly, while ground with manganese dioxide it runs briskly a couple of hundred degrees earlier, so the dioxide is written above the arrow as a condition and never balanced into the equation. And it truly is a catalyst here: unchanged in mass and in chemistry, it is recovered by dissolving the residue in water, filtering, washing and drying the solid — potassium chloride goes into solution, the dioxide does not — the plainest possible proof that a catalyst comes out intact. Three standing traps: potassium permanganate is no substitute for the dioxide, since it decomposes itself into three products and merely supplies the dioxide that does the catalysis afterwards; chlorate is a strong oxidiser and ground or warmed with charcoal, sulfur or paper it can flare or detonate, so it is mixed with nothing else; and the common miswrites are an unbalanced equation or the catalyst parked on the product side. Industry puts chlorate into match heads and pyrotechnics, the bench uses a spatula-tip, and what is left over never goes back into the bottle (see storing reagents and choosing the container).

subs.name: 碳酸钙（大理石/石灰石）
subs.note: 块状固体，与酸反应放气。
subs.noteEn: Lumpy solid; reacts with acid giving off gas.

subs.name: 稀盐酸
subs.note: 提供 H⁺ 与碳酸根反应。
subs.noteEn: Supplies H⁺ to react with carbonate.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 使澄清石灰水变浑浊，向上排空气法收集。
subs.noteEn: Turns limewater cloudy; collected by upward displacement of air.

term: 大理石与盐酸制二氧化碳
oneLiner: 大理石（碳酸钙）与稀盐酸反应制二氧化碳。
oneLinerEn: Marble (calcium carbonate) reacts with dilute HCl to give CO₂.
detail: 实验室制二氧化碳只用块状石灰石（或大理石）与稀盐酸，这三处“只用”都有理由，是考试最爱问的条件选择。第一，为什么不用稀硫酸？因为生成物硫酸钙微溶，会包裹在大理石表面把酸与碳酸钙隔开，反应几秒就自行停止（这与「酸雨与石灰石-石膏法脱硫」里硫酸钙成壳是同一件事），除非把石灰石磨成粉并不断搅拌。第二，为什么不用浓盐酸？因为它挥发出的氯化氢气体会混进二氧化碳，使收集的气体不纯，通入石灰水还会因酸性气体干扰而浑浊不明显。第三，为什么不用碳酸钠粉末？因为它与酸接触面积太大，一瞬间剧烈发泡，来不及收集；碳酸钠溶液是给“灭火器”和演示用的，不是制气的。装置走“固液不加热”，与制氢同一套；用向上排空气法收集，因为二氧化碳密度比空气大且能溶于水（常温约 1 体积水溶 1 体积气），一般不用排水法。验满的方法是把燃着的木条放在集气瓶口（不是伸进瓶里），火焰熄灭即满。反应的实质是碳酸钙与氢离子反应，写离子方程式时碳酸钙是固体不拆：CaCO₃ + 2H⁺ = Ca²⁺ + H₂O + CO₂↑，这一条同时说明“为什么碳酸盐都能与酸反应放出二氧化碳”——凡含碳酸根的都能提供 CO₃²⁻。二氧化碳的检验则走另一条特征反应：使澄清石灰水变浑浊（见「二氧化碳使石灰水变浑浊」）。工业上制二氧化碳反而常用高温煅烧石灰石这一分解反应，副产物就是生石灰（见「生石灰遇水」），一条碳酸钙的两条路正好互为对照。
detailEn: In the lab CO2 comes only from lump marble or limestone plus dilute hydrochloric acid, and each restriction has a reason worth reciting. Not dilute sulfuric acid: the CaSO4 formed is sparingly soluble and coats the marble, sealing acid away from carbonate so the reaction stalls after a few seconds - the same gypsum-shell effect as in Flue-Gas Desulfurisation - unless the stone is powdered and stirred. Not concentrated hydrochloric acid: its escaping HCl gas contaminates the CO2 and muddles the limewater test. Not sodium carbonate powder: the contact area is enormous, so it foams violently at once and the gas cannot be collected; the solution is reserved for fire extinguishers and demonstrations. The generator is again the solid-plus-liquid no-heat set shared with hydrogen, and collection is upward displacement of air because CO2 is denser than air and soluble in water (roughly one volume of water dissolves one volume of gas at room temperature), so drainage collection is normally not used. To check the jar is full, hold a burning splint at the mouth, not inside. The essence is carbonate meeting hydrogen ions; since CaCO3 is a solid it is not split apart in the ionic equation: CaCO3 + 2H+ = Ca2+ + H2O + CO2, which also explains why every carbonate fizzes with acid. Testing the gas is a different characteristic reaction - turbidity in limewater (see CO2 Turns Limewater Cloudy). Industry takes the opposite path, decomposing limestone at high temperature, whose co-product is quicklime (see Quicklime Meets Water), so the two routes through calcium carbonate make a neat pair.

subs.name: 水（加少量电解质）
subs.note: 被电解；加电解质增强导电性。

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 负极产生，可燃，体积约为氧气两倍。
subs.noteEn: At the cathode; flammable, about twice the O₂ volume.

oneLiner: 水电解生成氢气和氧气。
oneLinerEn: Water electrolyses into hydrogen and oxygen.
detail: 纯水几乎不导电，所以做这个实验要加少量稀硫酸或氢氧化钠溶液增强导电性；这里有个常见错误是加食盐，因为食盐水里的氯离子会在阳极先于氢氧根放电，放出的是氯气而不是氧气，两极产物全乱（原因见「电解池」的放电顺序）。操作时用直流电，两极均产生气泡，体积关系记成“正氧负氢、氢二氧一”：与电源正极相连的阳极得氧气、负极的阴极得氢气，体积比约 2（氢）比 1（氧）；检验办法是阴极气体靠近火焰有轻微爆鸣或安静燃烧，阳极气体使带火星木条复燃。注意体积比是 2 比 1，而质量比恰好反过来是 1 比 8（每 4 g 氢配 32 g 氧），因为一个氧分子是氢分子质量的 16 倍但只有一半的分子数。实测常发现氢气略多于两倍的氧，这不是错，而是因为氧气在水里的溶解度比氢气大一些，阳极本身也可能被氧化消耗掉一点氧。这条反应的论证价值在于“水由氢元素和氧元素组成”：分解与化合互为逆过程，它和「氢气燃烧」合起来才构成对水组成的完整证明，也是初中“化学变化中分子可分、原子不可分”的标准例证——水分子被拆成氢原子和氧原子，再两两组合成氢分子和氧分子，原子的种类和数目都没变。按电量算，生成 1 mol 氢气要通过 2 mol 电子，即约 19.3 万库仑（见「法拉第电解定律」），所以电解水制氢看着简单，工业上却是实打实的耗电大户，只有用廉价的可再生电力才谈得上“绿氢”。
detailEn: Pure water barely conducts, so a little dilute sulfuric acid or sodium hydroxide is added - and note the classic blunder of using table salt, because chloride discharges at the anode ahead of hydroxide and the gas is chlorine, not oxygen (the discharge order is laid out in Electrolytic Cell). With direct current both electrodes bubble; recite oxygen-at-anode, hydrogen-at-cathode, two to one by volume, so the anode gas relights a glowing splint and the cathode gas burns quietly or gives a small pop. The volume ratio is 2 to 1 but the mass ratio is the reverse, 1 to 8, because an oxygen molecule is sixteen times heavier while there are half as many of them. Measured hydrogen often exceeds exactly twice the oxygen, which is not an error: oxygen is somewhat more soluble in water than hydrogen, and the anode itself may consume a little. The argument this experiment supplies is the composition of water - decomposition and synthesis are reciprocal, and paired with Hydrogen Combustion they give the complete proof - and it is also the standard illustration that molecules divide in a chemical change while atoms do not: water molecules come apart into H and O atoms that re-pair into H2 and O2 with no atom lost or changed. By charge, making 1 mol of hydrogen needs 2 mol of electrons, roughly 193000 coulomb (see Faraday's Laws), which is why electrolytic hydrogen looks simple but is a serious electricity customer, economic only behind cheap renewable power.

subs.name: 铁（银白色金属）
subs.note: 较活泼，作还原剂置换铜。
subs.noteEn: More reactive; reduces and displaces copper.

subs.name: 硫酸铜（蓝色溶液）
subs.noteEn: Supplies the Cu²⁺ to be displaced.

subs.name: 硫酸亚铁（浅绿色溶液）
subs.noteEn: Solution fades from blue to pale green.

subs.name: 铜（红色固体）
subs.note: 析出附着于铁表面，湿法炼铜原理。
subs.noteEn: Deposits on the iron; the basis of hydrometallurgical copper.

term: 铁置换硫酸铜（湿法炼铜）
oneLiner: 铁把铜从硫酸铜溶液中置换出来。
oneLinerEn: Iron displaces copper from copper(II) sulfate solution.
detail: “曾青得铁则化为铜”是西汉炼丹著作里就写下的话，宋代用它从硫酸铜溶液（胆矾水）里炼铜，称为湿法炼铜——这是世界最早的炼铜法之一，原理就是这条置换反应。现象分三处观察：银白色的铁表面覆盖一层红色（紫红）固体，溶液由蓝色逐渐变浅绿色，若时间够长底部还有疏松的铜粉脱落。做实验前要用砂纸把铁丝打磨光亮，否则表面的氧化膜和油污会让现象来得很慢；判断反应是否完成看蓝色是否褪尽。这里最要紧的辨析是铁的价态：铁被铜离子氧化只能到 +2（生成 FeSO₄），不能一步跳到 +3，因为 Cu²⁺ 的氧化性不足以把铁推到三价；反过来，Fe³⁺ 却能把铜单质氧化溶解，2Fe³⁺ + Cu = 2Fe²⁺ + Cu²⁺，印刷电路板正是用氯化铁溶液“蚀刻”铜箔的。所以三价铁离子、铜离子、铜单质要按同一条氧化性强弱排序（Cu²⁺ 介于两者之间，见「氧化还原反应」）。差量计算也常考：每溶解 56 份质量的铁就析出 64 份质量的铜，固体增重 8 份、溶液相应减重 8 份，把铁钉浸入硫酸铜溶液后称量，总质量不变而铁钉变重，是典型的守恒加差量题。活动性顺序里排在铜前面的金属都能这样把铜置换出来（见「金属活动性顺序」），但要注意“钾钙钠扔进盐溶液先跟水反应”这条例外。今天湿法冶金仍在用同一原理，从矿山废水与电子废弃物浸出液里回收金属，是「电子废弃物提金（城市矿山）」路线的化学基础。
detailEn: The phrase if iron meets blue vitriol, copper is born comes from a Han-dynasty alchemical text, and by the Song dynasty it was used to recover copper from solutions of copper sulfate, the wet method - among the earliest hydrometallurgical routes anywhere. Read the phenomena in three places: a red-purple coating on the silvery iron, the blue solution fading to pale green, and after a long soak a loose powder of copper on the bottom. Sand the wire bright first, since oxide film and grease delay everything, and judge completion by whether any blue is left. The decisive subtlety is the valence of iron: Cu2+ is not oxidising enough to push iron straight to +3, so only FeSO4 forms; conversely Fe3+ does dissolve metallic copper, 2Fe3+ + Cu = 2Fe2+ + Cu2+, which is exactly how ferric chloride etches copper foil on printed circuit boards. Line up Fe3+, Cu2+ and Cu on one oxidising-strength ladder (see Redox Reactions), and note that mass-difference problems are classic: every 56 mass parts of iron dissolved deposits 64 parts of copper, so the solid gains 8 and the solution loses 8 - the whole beaker still weighs the same. Any metal above copper in the activity series can displace it this way (see the Metal Activity Series), except that potassium, calcium and sodium react with the water first. Modern dump-leach and e-waste recovery still rest on this reaction, the chemical base of urban mining.

subs.name: 锌粒
subs.note: 活泼金属，与稀酸反应放氢。
subs.noteEn: Reactive metal; gives H₂ with dilute acid.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 可燃，实验室制氢常用此法。
subs.noteEn: Flammable; a common lab route to H₂.

oneLiner: 锌与稀硫酸反应放出氢气。
oneLinerEn: Zinc reacts with dilute sulfuric acid to release H₂.
detail: 实验室制氢气就用锌粒与稀硫酸，选药品是一条一条比出来的：镁反应太快、热量大、气流难以控制，铁太慢而且往往因杂质发泡不止，铜在金属活动性顺序里排在氢之后、根本不反应，于是速率适中的锌成了标准选择（浓度常用 1:5 的稀硫酸，也可用稀盐酸，但盐酸挥发会让氢气带酸味）。真正的反应是金属与氢离子：Zn + 2H⁺ = Zn²⁺ + H₂↑，所以“金属失电子、氢离子得电子”是这一类反应的共同骨架，活泼性越强反应越快（见「金属活动性顺序」与「原电池」）。有两个坑必须提前踩掉。第一，只有稀的非氧化性酸（盐酸、稀硫酸）才放氢气；浓硫酸和硝酸是氧化性酸，与金属反应时得电子的是酸根里的中心原子，产物是二氧化硫或氮的氧化物而不是氢气，铜能溶在浓硫酸与硝酸里却溶不了在稀盐酸里，正是这条分界。第二，产氢量比较是“等质量金属与足量酸”还是“等量酸与足量金属”，两种题答案完全不同：前者比的是每克金属能给出几摩尔电子，即化合价除以相对原子质量，所以铝最多、镁次之、铁再次、锌最少（每克铝约 0.11 mol 电子、锌约 0.031 mol）；后者酸被用完，只要酸的量相同，最终生成的氢气一样多，只是快慢不同。顺手一个常考点：粗锌或滴几滴硫酸铜溶液反而反应更快，因为锌把铜置换出来贴在表面，锌-铜在酸里构成无数小原电池（呼应「原电池」的加速腐蚀），纯锌反而慢。
detailEn: Laboratory hydrogen is zinc granules plus dilute sulfuric acid, and that choice was argued item by item: magnesium is too fast and hot to control, iron too slow and prone to stubborn foaming from impurities, copper sits after hydrogen in the activity series and simply will not react, so moderate zinc wins, typically with 1:5 dilute sulfuric acid (dilute hydrochloric works but its fumes make the gas taste sour). The real reaction is metal against hydrogen ions, Zn + 2H+ = Zn2+ + H2, so metal loses electrons and hydrogen ions gain them in every member of this family, faster the more active the metal. Two traps to clear in advance. First, only dilute non-oxidising acids give hydrogen: with concentrated sulfuric acid or nitric acid the atom at the centre of the acid anion takes the electrons, so sulfur dioxide or nitrogen oxides come off instead - which is why copper dissolves in those two but not in hydrochloric acid. Second, be explicit about what is equal: equal masses of metal with excess acid ranks by electrons per gram, valence divided by relative atomic mass, so aluminium beats magnesium beats iron beats zinc (about 0.11 mol of electrons per gram for Al, 0.031 for Zn); equal amounts of acid with excess metal gives the same hydrogen either way, differing only in speed. A related exam point: coarse zinc, or a few drops of copper sulfate solution, reacts faster, because the cemented copper and zinc form countless microscopic galvanic cells in the acid (see Galvanic Cell), while pure zinc is sluggish.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 燃烧产物，使石灰水浑浊。

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 火焰上方冷烧杯内壁出现水珠。
subs.noteEn: Droplets condense on a cold beaker over the flame.

oneLiner: 甲烷在氧气中完全燃烧。
detail: 甲烷是天然气、沼气与“瓦斯”的主要成分，完全燃烧时火焰淡蓝、几乎无烟，所以它被认为是最干净的化石燃料——但这条“干净”有严格前提：必须完全燃烧，空气不足时同一份甲烷会生成一氧化碳甚至游离的碳（灶具火焰发黄、锅底起黑灰就是这个信号，此时应当调大进风口），而一氧化碳才是煤气中毒的元凶。检验产物是初中“由产物推组成”的标准套路：在火焰上方罩一个干而冷的烧杯，内壁凝出水珠说明产物有水、从而说明甲烷含氢元素；把烧杯倒转注入少量澄清石灰水振荡、变浑说明有二氧化碳、从而说明含碳元素。由质量守恒（反应前后元素种类不变）就能确定甲烷由碳和氢组成，这是“定性组成分析”最朴素的样板。量的关系也要读准：1 分子甲烷耗 2 分子氧、生成 1 分子二氧化碳和 2 分子水，所以每 1 体积甲烷约需 10 体积空气才能供足这 2 体积氧（氧气约占空气体积的五分之一）。安全上它和氢气一样“点燃前须验纯”：甲烷在空气中的爆炸极限约 5% 到 15%，矿井瓦斯爆炸、厨房泄漏爆炸都发生在这段浓度里，因此泄漏时不能开关电器、要先关阀开窗。热值方面，甲烷燃烧热约 890 kJ/mol，折合约 55.6 MJ/kg，高于汽油约 46 MJ/kg，且每单位热量排放的二氧化碳比煤和汽油都少，这是“以气代煤”的核心理由；但甲烷本身就是强温室气体，泄漏到大气中的增温能力远大于烧掉它排的那点二氧化碳，所以天然气的环保账必须算上输配环节的泄漏。
detailEn: Methane is the main constituent of natural gas, biogas and mine gas; burned completely it gives a pale blue, nearly smokeless flame, which is why it counts as the cleanest fossil fuel - but only under a strict condition: complete combustion. Starved of air the same methane yields carbon monoxide or free carbon, and a yellow flame with blacking on the pot bottom is the signal to open the air inlet; carbon monoxide is the actual culprit in gas poisoning. Verifying the products is the standard way of reasoning from products back to composition: hold a dry cold beaker over the flame, condensation inside proves water and therefore hydrogen in the fuel, then invert it with a little limewater, turbidity proves carbon dioxide and therefore carbon. Conservation of elements then settles the composition - the crudest and clearest model of qualitative analysis. Read the quantities exactly: one molecule of methane consumes two of oxygen and gives one of carbon dioxide plus two of water, so with oxygen at roughly a fifth of air, one volume of gas needs on the order of ten volumes of air. On safety it shares hydrogen's rule of testing purity before ignition: methane explodes between about 5 and 15 percent in air, so a leak must be handled by closing the valve and opening windows, never by switching appliances. Its heat of combustion is about 890 kJ per mole, some 55.6 MJ/kg, above gasoline's 46 MJ/kg, and it emits less carbon dioxide per joule than coal or petrol - the core case for switching to gas. Yet methane itself is a potent greenhouse gas, far stronger than the CO2 its burning releases, so the environmental ledger must count leakage along the distribution chain.

subs.name: 氢气
subs.note: 可燃气体，点燃前需验纯。
subs.noteEn: Flammable; must be tested for purity before ignition.

subs.name: 水
subs.note: 唯一产物，淡蓝色火焰、放热。

detail: 氢气燃烧是初中唯一要求亲手验证“产物只有水”的燃烧实验：在导管口点燃纯净的氢气，火焰呈淡蓝色（透过玻璃导管看时常带一点黄，要看清淡蓝可用干燥的玻璃片挡一下），火焰上方罩一个干而冷的烧杯，内壁立刻凝出水雾，说明产物只有水；用手摸烧杯外壁发烫，说明它放热。这条反应有三个用处。一、它是检验氢气最直观的方法，也是“水由氢和氧组成”的合成证据——与电解水正好互为逆过程，两条一起构成水的组成的完整论证。二、每摩尔氢气燃烧约放 286 kJ，按质量算热值高达约 143 MJ/kg，接近同质量汽油的三倍，而且产物只有水不排碳，所以它被当作燃料看待；难点全在储运，因为氢气密度最小，必须高压或液化才能装得下。三、它是“点燃前必须验纯”这条安全规矩的来源：氢气在空气里的体积分数约从 4% 到 75% 都属于爆炸极限，这一段内遇火都会爆炸，所以收集后先用小试管试爆——只听见一声闷响“噗”才算纯净，尖利的爆鸣说明还混着空气、必须重新收集。爆炸极限与「燃烧与灭火」里“有限空间内的剧烈燃烧就是爆炸”口径一致，而氢气还原氧化铜“先通氢、后点灯”的顺序也是同一个理由（见「置换反应」）。
detailEn: Burning hydrogen is the one combustion the junior course must verify by its product: light the pure gas at the jet, hold a dry cold beaker over the flame and mist forms on the wall at once, while the outside of the beaker turns warm. Three uses follow. It is the plainest test for hydrogen and the synthesis half of the argument that water is made of hydrogen and oxygen, electrolysis being the exact reverse — the two together settle the composition of water. It gives some 286 kJ per mole, roughly 143 MJ per kilogram, close to three times petrol, and its only product is water, so it is counted as a carbon-free fuel; the whole difficulty lies in carrying so light a gas about, which takes pressure or liquefaction. And it is why hydrogen must be proved pure before lighting: mixtures from about 4% to 75% by volume in air all explode on a flame, so a small tube is tested first — a soft 'pop' means pure, a sharp shriek means air is still in it and the collection must be repeated. That band is the explosive limit, kept to the same wording as the combustion and fire-control entry, and it is the same reason the copper-oxide reduction passes gas before the lamp is lit (see displacement).

subs.name: 水
subs.note: H⁺ 与 OH⁻ 结合；酚酞褪色指示终点。
subs.noteEn: H⁺ and OH⁻ combine; phenolphthalein fading marks the endpoint.

oneLiner: 盐酸与氢氧化钠中和生成盐和水。
oneLinerEn: Hydrochloric acid is neutralized by sodium hydroxide.
detail: 这条反应在烧杯里进行时什么也看不见——两种无色溶液混在一起还是无色，这正是中和滴定的第一个难点：必须借指示剂把看不见的等当点变成看得见的颜色变化。选酚酞而不是石蕊，是因为酚酞在约 pH 8.2 到 10 之间由红骤褪为无色，色变敏锐；石蕊是“紫到红、紫到蓝”的渐变，肉眼判断不出边界，教材里从不用它作滴定指示剂。操作手法有固定套路：左手控制滴定管活塞（或挤压玻璃珠）、右手摇动锥形瓶、眼睛注视瓶内颜色而不是刻度；接近终点时改成半滴半滴加，用锥形瓶内壁把半滴蹭下去。终点判定：滴到最后一滴使溶液由浅红恰好变为无色、且半分钟内不复原。要清楚这个终点严格说在微碱性一侧（pH 约 8.2 时酚酞才褪色），此时还剩极少量氢氧化钠没被中和，但因为强酸强碱滴定在等当点附近 pH 会发生“突跃”（半滴之差从 pH 10 掉到 4），这点误差落在允许范围内——这也是为什么不能用它来滴定很弱的酸或碱，突跃不明显就无法选对指示剂。反应的实质是 H⁺ + OH⁻ = H₂O，生成的 NaCl 只是留在溶液里的“旁观者”，所以蒸发结晶才得到食盐晶体（见「分离与提纯的方法及仪器配套」）。“中和”两个字的边界也要划清：并非所有酸与碱的反应都只生成盐和水，碳酸钠与盐酸会放气、酸与金属氧化物反应生成盐和水却不属于中和（中和的定义是酸与碱作用），这些在「碳酸钠与盐酸」与「酸碱」两条里各自说明。放热与 57.3 kJ/mol 的定量口径见「中和热」，胃里的中和见「胃酸中和（胃药）」。
detailEn: Carried out in a beaker this reaction shows nothing: two colourless solutions give a colourless mixture, which is the first difficulty of titration - the equivalence point is invisible until an indicator turns it into colour. Phenolphthalein is chosen over litmus because it drops from red to colourless sharply across about pH 8.2 to 10, whereas litmus fades gradually and no eye can call its boundary; textbooks never titrate with it. The technique is fixed: left hand on the stopcock, right hand swirling the flask, eyes watching the colour in the flask rather than the scale; near the end point add half-drops and wash them off the wall. Judge the end point as the last drop leaving the solution colourless with no pink returning within half a minute. Strictly, that end point sits on the mildly alkaline side, since phenolphthalein only pales at about pH 8.2, so a trace of sodium hydroxide survives - acceptable because a strong acid against a strong base jumps from about pH 10 to 4 within half a drop, and that is exactly why the same indicator choice fails for very weak acids or bases, where no such jump exists. The essence is H+ + OH- = H2O, with NaCl only a spectator left in solution, so evaporating to dryness is what yields the salt crystals (see Choosing a Separation Method). Mark the borders of the word neutralise as well: not every acid-base reaction gives only salt and water - sodium carbonate with acid fizzes, and an acid dissolving a metal oxide gives salt and water yet is not neutralisation, which by definition is acid plus base. Numbers and heat belong to Heat of Neutralisation, the stomach version to Antacid Chemistry.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 大量放气，泡沫灭火器原理之一。

oneLiner: 碳酸钠与盐酸反应放出二氧化碳。
oneLinerEn: Sodium carbonate reacts with HCl, releasing CO₂.
detail: 这条方程式看着与「大理石与盐酸制二氧化碳」同型，但真正的考点藏在滴加顺序里，而它同时也是不另加试剂区分碳酸钠溶液与稀盐酸的经典方法（互滴法）。把盐酸逐滴加入碳酸钠溶液：开始时一点气泡都没有，因为碳酸根先只结合一个氢离子变成碳酸氢根，CO₃²⁻ + H⁺ = HCO₃⁻；等碳酸根被全部转化，继续滴酸才突然大量放气，HCO₃⁻ + H⁺ = H₂O + CO₂↑。反过来把碳酸钠溶液滴入过量盐酸：一接触立刻剧烈冒泡，因为每一滴碳酸根遇到的都是充足的氢离子。同两种药品、顺序不同、现象完全不同，这就是“量与顺序决定产物”的标准案例：1 比 1 时得到碳酸氢钠（Na₂CO₃ + HCl = NaHCO₃ + NaCl），1 比 2 时才走完总反应。所以“等质量的碳酸钠与碳酸氢钠分别与足量盐酸反应”这类比较题，必须先分清问的是耗酸量还是放气量：碳酸钠每 106 g 放 44 g 二氧化碳而耗 2 mol 盐酸，碳酸氢钠每 84 g 就放 44 g 二氧化碳而只耗 1 mol，单位质量的碳酸氢钠放气更多、单位二氧化碳对应的酸更少。另外三个必须钉住的点：一、碳酸钠俗名纯碱、苏打，但它属于盐而不是碱，水溶液因水解显碱性（见「盐类水解」），“纯碱不是碱”是「常见物质的俗名与主要成分」里最经典的一条；二、焰色反应呈黄色是钠盐的身份证，验证时用铂丝或无锈铁丝蘸稀盐酸灼烧至无色再蘸样品，透过蓝色钴玻璃看是排除钾的干扰；三、泡沫灭火器实际用的是碳酸氢钠浓溶液与硫酸铝溶液双水解（两者互相促进放出大量二氧化碳并形成氢氧化铝泡沫膜，见「盐类水解」），而不是这条碳酸钠与盐酸的反应，别把两者混为一谈。
detailEn: The equation looks like a twin of CO2 from Carbonate, but the point hides in the order of addition, which is also the classic way to tell the two solutions apart with no third reagent (cross-drop test). Add acid dropwise into sodium carbonate solution and nothing bubbles at first, because carbonate only accepts one proton and becomes bicarbonate, CO3(2-) + H+ = HCO3-; gas erupts only after all carbonate has been converted and the next protons meet bicarbonate. Reverse it - pour carbonate solution into excess acid - and every drop fizzes instantly, since each CO3(2-) finds protons plentiful. Same two bottles, opposite appearance, the standard lesson that quantities and order decide products: 1 to 1 stops at sodium hydrogen carbonate (Na2CO3 + HCl = NaHCO3 + NaCl), 1 to 2 runs the whole way. So for comparisons of equal masses of carbonate and bicarbonate with excess acid, first ask whether the question is acid consumed or gas released: 106 g of carbonate gives 44 g of CO2 while needing 2 mol of HCl, whereas 84 g of bicarbonate gives the same 44 g on only 1 mol - bicarbonate wins per gram, carbonate costs more acid per litre of gas. Three facts worth nailing: sodium carbonate is called soda or washing soda yet is a salt, not a base, alkaline only through hydrolysis (see Salt Hydrolysis), the most quoted entry in Common Names and Formulas; a yellow flame test is sodium's ID card, wire cleaned in hydrochloric acid and viewed through cobalt blue glass to exclude potassium; and foam fire extinguishers actually use concentrated sodium hydrogen carbonate with aluminium sulfate, mutual hydrolysis releasing gas and an aluminium hydroxide foam blanket, not this reaction.

subs.name: 熟石灰/消石灰
subs.note: 反应放热，用于建筑与干燥。
subs.noteEn: Exothermic product; used in building and drying.

oneLiner: 生石灰与水化合生成熟石灰。
oneLinerEn: Quicklime combines with water to form slaked lime.
detail: 把水倒进生石灰，几秒内块体崩解成粉末、冒出大量白色蒸汽、用手摸外壁烫得握不住——这是初中化学里放热最剧烈、也是最容易被安全忽视的一个化合反应，1 mol 氧化钙与水化合约放出 64 kJ，足以让一部分水沸腾，所以“自热米饭”的加热包、冬天烘手的石灰袋用的都是它；食品袋里那小包写“不可食用、勿入水”的干燥剂就是它，撕开或加水会灼伤，这是这条反应最实际的生活考点。产物氢氧化钙叫熟石灰或消石灰，加水得到的悬浊液是石灰乳、澄清的饱和溶液才是石灰水（注意：石灰水是稀溶液，氢氧化钙微溶，20 ℃ 时 100 g 水只溶约 0.16 g，这就是“为什么吸收二氧化碳要用氢氧化钠而检验才用石灰水”的原因，见「二氧化碳使石灰水变浑浊」）。生石灰作干燥剂只能干燥中性或碱性气体，如氧气、氢气、氨气，绝不能用它干燥二氧化碳、二氧化硫、氯化氢这些酸性气体，因为它们会与氧化钙或生成的氢氧化钙反应而被吃掉——干燥剂的选择看“是否与气体反应”，不看能不能吸水。整条线是初中最重要的“钙三角”：石灰石高温煅烧得生石灰（分解反应）、生石灰加水得熟石灰（化合、放热）、熟石灰吸收空气里的二氧化碳又变回碳酸钙（这也是石灰浆墙面硬化、抹的灰墙“出汗”的原因），三步把 CaCO₃、CaO、Ca(OH)₂ 串成一圈，配平与类型判断的题基本都绕这一圈出。此外熟石灰的两种工业用法都靠它的碱性：中和酸性土壤与酸性废水（比用氢氧化钠便宜且温和），以及与硫酸铜溶液配波尔多液杀菌剂。
detailEn: Pour water on quicklime and within seconds the lumps collapse into powder, white vapour pours off and the vessel is too hot to hold: the most violent exothermic combination in secondary-school chemistry and the one most often taken unsafely. About 64 kJ per mole of CaO is released, enough to boil part of the water, which is why self-heating rice packs and hand warmers use it, and why the little desiccant sachet marked do not eat, keep dry is dangerous once torn open or wetted. The product Ca(OH)2 is slaked or hydrated lime; mixed with water it gives milk of lime, and only the clear saturated layer is limewater - a dilute solution, since slaked lime is sparingly soluble, about 0.16 g per 100 g of water at 20 degrees, which is precisely why sodium hydroxide, not lime, is used to absorb carbon dioxide industrially (see CO2 Turns Limewater Cloudy). As a drying agent quicklime may serve neutral or basic gases such as oxygen, hydrogen and ammonia, but never acidic gases like carbon dioxide, sulfur dioxide or hydrogen chloride, which it would consume: the choice of a drying agent turns on reaction with the gas, not on thirst. This line completes the calcium triangle - calcining limestone decomposes it to CaO, adding water combines back to the hydroxide, and the hydroxide takes CO2 from air to return to CaCO3, which is also why freshly limewashed walls sweat and then harden. The two industrial uses of slaked lime both exploit its base strength: neutralising acidic soil and acidic wastewater, cheaper and gentler than sodium hydroxide, and, with copper sulfate solution, the fungicide Bordeaux mixture.

subs.name: 澄清石灰水（氢氧化钙溶液）
碳酸钙（白色沉淀）
subs.note: 使溶液变浑浊，CO₂ 的特征现象。
subs.noteEn: Clouds the solution; the signature test for CO₂.

term: 二氧化碳使石灰水变浑浊
oneLiner: 二氧化碳通入澄清石灰水生成白色沉淀。
oneLinerEn: Carbon dioxide turns limewater cloudy with a white precipitate.
detail: 使澄清石灰水变浑浊是二氧化碳的“特征反应”，但这句话有两个必须补全的边界。第一，检验与除杂是两回事：氢氧化钙微溶，20 ℃ 时 100 g 水只溶约 0.16 g，石灰水太稀，用来吸收（除去）混合气里的二氧化碳效果很差，除杂要改用氢氧化钠浓溶液；反过来说，因为浑浊来得显眼、又是钙盐的特征现象，检验才非它不可。所以“用石灰水检验、用氢氧化钠吸收”是一对必须成对记住的分工，也解释了为什么瓶壁长期涂石灰水保鲜鸡蛋反而能让蛋壳加厚（呼出的二氧化碳不断生成碳酸钙）。第二，浑浊不是二氧化碳独有的：二氧化硫作为酸性氧化物走完全平行的路，SO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ = CaSO₃↓ + H₂O，同样出白色沉淀，因此“通入石灰水变浑就断定是二氧化碳”是错误推理，混合气里若可能含二氧化硫要用品红溶液先确认再判断（见「常见气体的检验与验满」）。第三个层次是同一条反应的两面：持续通入过量二氧化碳，浑浊会重新变澄清，因为碳酸钙与水、二氧化碳结合成可溶的碳酸氢钙，CaCO₃ + H₂O + CO₂ = Ca(HCO₃)₂；把这份澄清液加热，碳酸氢钙分解、二氧化碳跑掉，白色沉淀又回来了。自然界里石灰岩溶洞与钟乳石正是这一进一退亿万年的结果——含二氧化碳的雨水溶解石灰岩形成碳酸氢钙溶液，滴落洞顶时二氧化碳逸出、碳酸钙重新沉积。第四，实验要求用新制的澄清石灰水，久置的会在液面结一层白膜（已经和空气里的二氧化碳反应完了），灵敏度大打折扣；这层白膜本身恰好证明空气中确实含有二氧化碳。
detailEn: Turning clear limewater cloudy is the characteristic reaction of carbon dioxide, but the sentence needs two boundaries. First, testing and scrubbing are different jobs: calcium hydroxide is sparingly soluble, only about 0.16 g per 100 g of water at 20 degrees, so limewater is far too dilute to strip CO2 from a gas stream - concentrated sodium hydroxide solution does that - while the test needs limewater precisely because the turbidity is loud and specific. Remember the pair as one rule: test with lime, absorb with soda. Second, cloudiness is not unique to CO2: sulfur dioxide, also an acidic oxide, runs an identical path, SO2 + Ca(OH)2 = CaSO3 + H2O, so concluding carbon dioxide from turbidity alone is a false inference; if sulfur dioxide may be present, confirm it first with fuchsin solution (see Testing Gases and Checking the Jar Is Full). Third, the same equilibrium has two faces: pass excess CO2 and the precipitate redissolves as soluble calcium hydrogen carbonate, CaCO3 + H2O + CO2 = Ca(HCO3)2; warm that clear liquid and the bicarbonate breaks down, releasing CO2 and bringing the white solid back. Cave stalactites are this give and take over geological time - rainwater charged with CO2 dissolves limestone, and at the drip the gas escapes and carbonate redeposits. Fourth, use freshly prepared limewater: a standing bottle skins over with calcium carbonate, already spent and much less sensitive, though that film itself proves carbon dioxide is present in air.

subs.name: 水（潮湿环境）
subs.note: 形成电解质膜，促成电化学腐蚀。
subs.noteEn: Forms an electrolyte film enabling electrochemical corrosion.

subs.name: 铁锈（红棕色疏松固体）
subs.note: 主要成分为氧化铁水合物，疏松不能保护内部铁。
subs.noteEn: Hydrated iron(III) oxide; porous, so it cannot protect the metal beneath.

oneLiner: 铁在潮湿空气中发生吸氧腐蚀生锈。
oneLinerEn: Iron corrodes in moist air (oxygen absorption).
detail: 铁生锈的条件不是“水”也不是“氧气”，而是两者同时在场，这一点靠一组三管对照实验钉死：第一管放干燥剂与烘干的铁钉（有氧气、无水）不锈，第二管用煮沸后迅速冷却的蒸馏水浸没铁钉并在水面加一层植物油隔绝空气（有水、几乎无氧气）也不锈，第三管铁钉半浸在普通食盐水或自来水里则锈得最明显。结论写完整应是“铁与空气中的氧气、水共同作用”，只答其一不得分。方程式里的 2xH₂O 与产物 Fe₂O₃·xH₂O 中的 x 表示“水量不定”，它是组成记号而不是配平系数，不能拿它去算物质的量——这条方程式重在说明铁锈的主体是三氧化二铁的水合物。机理上这是电化学腐蚀，即微型原电池在工作：负极是铁失电子，Fe − 2e⁻ = Fe²⁺，正极上氧气在酸性很弱或中性的水膜里得电子，O₂ + 2H₂O + 4e⁻ = 4OH⁻，所以叫吸氧腐蚀；生成的亚铁离子继续被氧气氧化并脱水，最终变成含三价铁的红棕色铁锈。食盐水、酸性雨、工业废气让水膜导电性变强，因而显著加速——这也是海边钢架、桥梁与自行车链条最容易烂的原因；若水膜酸性较强，正极就换成析氢腐蚀（见「金属的腐蚀与防护」）。铁锈疏松多孔，会把水汽吸进来让腐蚀一层层向内进行到底，这与铝截然不同：铝表面生成的氧化铝致密、把金属封住，所以“铝比铁活泼却更耐腐蚀”是同一份答案的两半。防护办法都围绕切断条件：刷漆、涂油、搪瓷、烤蓝形成屏障；镀锌（白铁）即使镀层破损，锌作为负极先被腐蚀而铁被保护，叫牺牲阳极；镀锡（马口铁）破损后反而铁先烂，因为铁成了负极——两种罐头皮的取向完全相反，是原电池原理最实用的例证。船体水线以下挂锌块、地下管道通外加电流都属同一类，代价上全球每年因腐蚀损失约相当于生产总值的 3% 到 4%。
detailEn: Rusting needs neither water alone nor oxygen alone but both at once, and a three-tube control fixes this: a dried nail with desiccant (oxygen, no water) stays bright; a nail under boiled-then-cooled distillate sealed by a layer of oil (water, almost no oxygen) also stays; a half-immersed nail in tap or salt water rusts fastest. State the conclusion in full - iron acting with both oxygen and water - or the answer loses marks. The 2xH2O on the left and Fe2O3·xH2O on the right use x for variable water content, a composition symbol and not a balancing coefficient that can be quantified; the equation's job is to say rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide. The mechanism is electrochemical corrosion, a miniature galvanic cell: iron loses electrons at the anode, Fe - 2e- = Fe2+, while oxygen gains them in the neutral or weakly acidic film, O2 + 2H2O + 4e- = 4OH-, hence oxygen-absorption corrosion; the ferrous ion is then oxidised further and dehydrates into red-brown rust containing iron(III). Salt water, acid rain and industrial fumes make the film more conductive and accelerate it sharply, which is why seaside steelwork, bridges and bicycle chains fail first; in a strongly acidic film the cathode reaction switches to hydrogen evolution (see Corrosion and Protection). Rust is porous and holds moisture, so corrosion burrows inward to the last gram, whereas alumina on aluminium is dense and seals the metal - one answer, two halves, for why the more reactive aluminium outlasts iron. Every defence cuts a condition: paint, grease, enamel, bluing as barriers; galvanising (zinc) protects even through a scratch because zinc becomes the sacrificial anode, while tin plate, once breached, lets iron corrode because iron is then the anode - two food cans pointing opposite ways, the most practical demonstration of the galvanic principle. Zinc blocks on hulls and impressed current on buried pipelines belong to the same family, and corrosion costs the world roughly 3 to 4 percent of output each year.

subs.name: 硫酸钡（白色沉淀）
subs.note: 不溶于稀硝酸，SO₄²⁻ 的特征检验。
subs.noteEn: Insoluble in dilute nitric acid; the signature test for SO₄²⁻.

oneLiner: 氯化钡与硫酸生成白色硫酸钡沉淀。
oneLinerEn: Barium chloride gives a white BaSO₄ precipitate with sulfuric acid.
detail: “先加稀盐酸、再加氯化钡溶液”——这一句是检验硫酸根的全部答案，顺序与试剂都不能替换，因为每一步都在排除一个假阳性。先加稀盐酸的目的有三：一是排除碳酸根与亚硫酸根，它们与钡离子同样生成白色沉淀 BaCO₃、BaSO₃，但都能溶于盐酸而消失（“三出口”里的沉淀在酸里化掉了，见「复分解反应」）；二是排除银离子，若溶液里有 Ag⁺，加盐酸立刻产生不溶于稀硝酸的白色氯化银沉淀，先加酸就能提前发现并另作处理；三是把溶液调成酸性环境，使后面生成的硫酸钡沉淀得更完全。再加氯化钡出现白色沉淀、且沉淀不溶于稀盐酸，才可以说含 SO₄²⁻，反应为 Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ = BaSO₄↓。因此两个常见错误做法必须点名：其一，只加氯化钡不加酸，可能被碳酸钡或氯化银误判；其二，改用稀硝酸酸化——稀硝酸（以及酸性条件下的硝酸根）有强氧化性，会把亚硫酸根氧化成硫酸根，于是原溶液明明只有亚硫酸根也会“检出”硫酸钡沉淀，这是最典型的假阳性来源，所以试剂要选盐酸与氯化钡，绝不能用硝酸钡代替氯化钡。BaSO₄ 的溶度积极小（约 1.1×10⁻¹⁰ 量级），既不溶于水也不溶于酸，这正是它能作“钡餐”的原因：不溶解就不会释放有毒的钡离子，因此医院用硫酸钡做消化道造影；反过来碳酸钡溶于胃酸，误食会中毒，急救办法是口服硫酸钠（或硫酸镁）溶液，把它转成不溶的硫酸钡（见「药品的存放与容器选择」）。定量上，硫酸钡重量法是测定硫或钡的经典办法：过滤、洗涤至无氯离子、灼烧恒重后称量，沉淀中钡与硫的固定比例（233 份对 32 份）就是计算依据。检验亚硫酸根反而要靠“加酸放出能使品红褪色的气体”，别把两者弄混（见「常见离子的检验」）。
detailEn: Take a sample, add dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride solution - those few words are the whole answer for testing sulfate, and neither the order nor the reagents are swappable, because each step removes a false positive. Dilute hydrochloric acid first does three jobs: it eliminates carbonate and sulfite, which also give white precipitates with barium but dissolve in acid (the same acid-soluble exit of double decomposition); it exposes silver ion, since Ag+ throws down white silver chloride insoluble in dilute nitric acid and can be caught before the real test; and it fixes an acidic medium where barium sulfate precipitates most completely. Only then does a white precipitate, insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid, prove SO4(2-): Ba2+ + SO4(2-) = BaSO4. Name the two wrong procedures. Adding barium chloride without acid can be fooled by barium carbonate or silver chloride. Acidifying with dilute nitric acid is worse, since nitric acid and nitrate under acidic conditions are strong oxidisers that convert sulfite to sulfate, so a solution containing only sulfite will faithfully report barium sulfate - the classic false positive, and the reason barium nitrate must never substitute for barium chloride. BaSO4 has a very small solubility product, on the order of 1.1e-10, and dissolves neither in water nor in acid, which is exactly why it is safe as the contrast medium swallowed for gastrointestinal X-rays: nothing dissolves, no toxic barium ion is released. Barium carbonate, by contrast, dissolves in stomach acid and poisons, and the antidote is drinking sodium or magnesium sulfate solution to convert it into the insoluble salt. Gravimetrically, barium sulfate weighing is the classical determination of sulfur or barium: filter, wash free of chloride, ignite to constant mass, and compute from the fixed ratio 233 to 32. Testing sulfite is a different act - acidify and smell the gas that bleaches fuchsin - so do not confuse the two.

subs.name: 二氧化碳
subs.note: 使面团疏松膨大，膨松剂原理。

oneLiner: 碳酸氢钠受热分解放出二氧化碳。
oneLinerEn: Sodium bicarbonate decomposes on heating, releasing CO₂.
detail: 这是鉴别碳酸钠与碳酸氢钠最省事的一条实验：把固体装入干燥试管、管口略向下倾斜，加热后将气体通入澄清石灰水，石灰水变浑且管口内壁出现水珠，就说明样品是碳酸氢钠；而碳酸钠同样强热几乎没有任何变化（它要熔化到极高温度才分解）。所以“热稳定性对照”是这对俗名兄弟最干脆的区分法，也是“纯碱与小苏打”在「常见物质的俗名与主要成分」里必须连带记住的一条。装置的两个细节都是防倒流与防炸裂：管口向下是因为反应生成水，固体加热时冷凝水若倒流回灼热管底会炸裂；收集完要先把导管移开液面再熄灯（与「高锰酸钾受热分解」同一规矩）。量的关系值得算一次：每 168 g 碳酸氢钠放出 44 g 二氧化碳、并留下 106 g 碳酸钠；同样质量的碳酸钠则一点气体都不给。因此作膨松剂时碳酸氢钠的“单位质量放气量”更高，但单独用它有个缺陷——残留的碳酸钠显碱性，会让糕点发黄、有碱味甚至发苦，所以市售泡打粉是复配产品：小苏打加上酒石酸氢钾或磷酸二氢钙等酸性成分，遇水先放一部分气（酸碱中和）、烘烤时再放一部分（受热分解），两段放气让组织均匀，这也是「碳酸钠与盐酸」里“顺序与用量决定产物”的厨房版。医疗上它也用于中和过多胃酸，但代价是立刻在胃里生成二氧化碳，会胀气、嗳气，胃溃疡患者有穿孔风险，所以现代胃药更常用氢氧化铝或氢氧化镁（见「胃酸中和（胃药）」）。工业上它还是侯氏制碱法里第一个结晶析出的产物——正因为它在氨盐水中溶解度相对最小（见「侯氏制碱法」），而“碳酸氢钠溶液显碱性却属于酸式盐”这一点，也常在「酸碱」“俗名”两格里被考到。
detailEn: This is the laziest reliable way to tell soda from baking soda: heat the dry solid in a tube tilted mouth-down, pass the gas into limewater; clouding plus droplets inside the mouth proves sodium hydrogen carbonate, while sodium carbonate under the same strong heat barely changes, needing far higher temperatures to decompose. That thermal-stability contrast is the cleanest divider for this pair of common names, and belongs attached to Soda vs Baking Soda in Common Names and Formulas. Two apparatus details both fight backflow: the tilt is needed because the reaction makes water, and condensate running onto the hot bottom would crack the tube; and the delivery tube must leave the liquid before the lamp goes out, the same rule as Potassium Permanganate Decomposition. Worth one calculation: every 168 g of bicarbonate releases 44 g of CO2 and leaves 106 g of carbonate, whereas the same mass of carbonate yields no gas at all. So per gram bicarbonate raises more, yet used alone it leaves a flaw - the sodium carbonate residue is alkaline, yellowing the crumb and giving a soapy bitter taste, which is why commercial baking powder is compounded: soda cream plus an acid salt such as potassium hydrogen tartrate or monocalcium phosphate, giving one burst of gas when wet (acid meeting base) and a second on heating (thermal decomposition), two-stage leavening for an even crumb, the kitchen echo of order and quantity deciding products in Na2CO3 + HCl. Medically it neutralises excess stomach acid but generates carbon dioxide inside the stomach, causing bloating and belching with a perforation risk in ulcers, so modern antacids prefer aluminium or magnesium hydroxide (see Antacid Chemistry). Industrially it is the first crystal to appear in the Hou process precisely because it is the least soluble in the ammoniated brine (see Hou's Process), and the fact that its solution is alkaline although it is an acid salt keeps appearing in the Acids and Bases and common-name entries.
